name: closing
description: Final slide. Dark canvas mirror of title.
purpose: Last slide of every deck. Restates the takeaway or call-to-action. Drops the page number and keeps the deck's header and footer, by the anchor-chrome rule (engineering/decisions/2026-11-08-anchor-chrome.md) — the dark canvas signals "we're done." Add `spectrum` (mirrors `title`'s) when the deck itself is built on a multi-step color story worth echoing on the way out. The deck's `cover: light` register repaints the front and back cover together on the deck's light canvas, in both color modes (`cover-light`; a slide opts out with `cover-inverse`). `light` alone sets a scheme and keeps the dark panel (lib/base/base.registers.docs.md § cover). Seven cover compositions (`cover-masthead`, `cover-ledger`, `cover-column`, `cover-label`, `cover-stage`, `cover-frame`, `cover-poster`) set how the heading block sits; the deck writes one with the same register's second word (`cover: light column`) so both covers match, and `cover-plain` keeps one slide centered. A `cover-stage` or `cover-poster` heading holds about 60 characters; a longer one grows down from the top of the frame and overflows at the foot.

heading.description:
Closing line — takeaway, thank-you, or call to action. Capped at `--measure-bookend-heading` (16em ≈ 33 characters), mirroring title; `text-wrap: balance` evens the lines. Override the token in front-matter `style:` — never hand-break with `
`.

subtitle.description: Optional supporting line. Capped at `--measure-bookend-lede` (26em ≈ 56 characters) — a reading measure, so a two-clause sign-off holds together instead of running the frame's ~90 characters. A trailing list's rows take the same measure.

whenToUse.title: Last slide of every deck
whenToUse.body: Closes the bookend pair with title. Restates the takeaway, the call to action, or the next-steps line. The dark canvas tells the audience visually that the presentation is over.

whenToUse.title: Single takeaway line
whenToUse.body: The h2 is the slide. Keep it to one editorial line that summarizes the whole deck or names the action the audience should take. The eyebrow can carry a sub-line or link.

whenToUse.title: Accent modifier for emphasis
whenToUse.body: Pair with the universal `accent` modifier to recolor the focal heading. Useful when the closing line is a quote or a key decision the deck has been building toward.

antiPatterns.title: Multi-line heading
antiPatterns.body: Keep the closing line to one editorial sentence. The layout is centered and large — two-line closings get cramped and lose impact.

antiPatterns.title: Header or footer overrides
antiPatterns.body: Don't blank the footer with `_footer: ''` on the closing: it is the deck's standing note (a "Confidential", a copyright), and the last slide is often the one left on screen. Drop it on purpose with `no-footer`, or every band with `silent`.

antiPatterns.title: Mid-deck closing
antiPatterns.body: If the audience needs a strong statement mid-deck, use `big-number` or `content` with the `dark` modifier. Reserving closing for the final slide preserves its bookend role.

related.name: title

related.when: mid-deck section breaks — same dark canvas

related.when: single emphatic statement mid-deck without the bookend signal

commonMistakes.mistake: Eyebrow written as bold or plain text instead of inline code.
commonMistakes.fix: The eyebrow match is `h2 + p:has(> code:only-child)` — wrap it in backticks immediately after the heading; without the code span it falls through to the general italic subtitle rule instead of the eyebrow lifted above the heading.

commonMistakes.mistake: The subtitle paragraph is authored before the eyebrow paragraph instead of after it.
commonMistakes.fix: The eyebrow match is an immediate-next-ELEMENT-sibling selector (`h2 + p:has(> code:only-child)`) — keep the source order heading → eyebrow → subtitle.

commonMistakes.mistake: In the `index` variant, the leading reference key isn't wrapped in inline code, e.g. `docs — the component catalog` instead of leading with a backtick-wrapped key.
commonMistakes.fix: The `index` variant's mono reference-key styling (`section.closing.index :is(ul,ol) li code`) only applies to an actual `<code>` element — wrap the leading key in backticks so it renders as a mono chip, not plain text.

variantDecisionRule.useWhen: A single-sentence takeaway or call-to-action closes the deck — the common case.
The audience should leave with a scannable link (docs URL, contact card) rather than just a text call-to-action.
The closing is a reference/see-also list of multiple next steps or resources, not a single takeaway sentence.
`title` also carries `spectrum` — closes the bookend pair with the same generated gradient bar, echoing the deck's own multi-step color story one last time.
A heavy rule over the title, set left: the editorial cover. Usually set deck-wide with `cover: masthead`, so the front cover matches.
A small-caps title over a double rule: the annual-report cover. Usually set deck-wide with `cover: ledger`, so the front cover matches.
An accent column at the right edge, clear of the chrome bands; the title is set left and wraps short of it. Usually set deck-wide with `cover: column`, so the front cover matches.
A gallery wall label: the title in the slide-title size, low on the left, under a hairline, with a quiet caption. Usually set deck-wide with `cover: label`, so the front cover matches.
The title at stage size, centered: the display role, for a keynote room. Usually set deck-wide with `cover: stage`, so the front cover matches.
The title boxed in a keyline that follows the preset's rule weight and style. Usually set deck-wide with `cover: frame`, so the front cover matches.
A giant title set left, heavy and tight: the poster cover. Usually set deck-wide with `cover: poster`, so the front cover matches.
